first.rationale: Two of the three current pressures (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) point to the same funnel weakness, and memory_31/memory_86 both report durable, low-risk lifts from onboarding/signup simplification without noted harm to revenue quality. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor threat, but its record only documents short-term acquisition/revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs, with no confirmation of long-term retention or qualified-revenue quality — matching a customer segment already prone to churn to whoever is cheapest. Reacting to a pricing war with our one experiment slot risks training our funnel toward low-LTV accounts, undermining the 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective. I want to verify the original records for memory_86 and memory_31 specifically to confirm the activation/onboarding lifts were measured on genuine downstream engagement (not just top-of-funnel signups) before committing capacity, and to check whether simplification had any hidden cost to lead qualification that later analysts might have observed. Given only one experiment this week and no rollback, I'm scoping it as a small guarded test on the self-serve onboarding flow rather than a broad rollout, so we can observe whether the lift holds under current competitive and activation pressure before scaling.

final.rationale: The archive confirms exp_86 cleanly: shortening onboarding lifted completion +13%, cut time-to-value by 2.1 days, and *improved* 30-day retention +3% β€” a rare case where a funnel change helped both speed and downstream quality with no tradeoff. This directly targets the current 4% QoQ onboarding completion decline and plausibly the activation dip too, since faster time-to-value should feed activation. By contrast, exp_31 (signup simplification) is confirmed only for SMB, shows a small retention dip (-1%), and explicitly did not replicate on other segments β€” a weaker, narrower, and slightly riskier basis for this week's single experiment, especially with a competitor already pulling on SMB price sensitivity; stacking another SMB-specific lever with a retention cost seemed unwise. Promotional pricing remains unverified and, per memory_73, only documents short-term acquisition/revenue lift without retention/LTV data, which is the wrong tool against a price war if it erodes qualified revenue quality. I'm committing the week's slot to onboarding shortening, scoped as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) since the original result is well-confirmed but conditions have shifted (competitive pressure, broader activation decline) and I want to verify the lift replicates now before scaling further. Uncertainty is preserved: we don't yet know if today's stressed environment reproduces exp_86's retention gains, and the competitor pricing threat still needs a separate future response.
